findings.evidence: The 2026-10-31 run (commit 6f9237525) passed its preflight for all 110 cells between 01:57 and 02:06, Flash-Next's long-form guard among them ('validate -run -preflight 35/110 ... no models loaded or measured during setup; preflight: ready, nothing measured'), because Ready is called before any model is loaded or the device opened. ERROR physical GPU memory admission: insufficient device capacity: requested 48 bytes; available 0' (overgo_data/scratch/measure-run-20261031b.log, lines 915 to 924). Flash-Next's serving, ifeval, bbh and mmlu-pro cells in the same run are not broken, so the break is the long-form guard's own device memory, which one load and one request at its largest rung shows in about a minute. In the 2026-10-30 run the same cell was broken by a missing short-prompt benchmark and reported among the broken cells at the run's end. A break it finds stops the run there, names the model and the message, and is filed as a row; with SQA-267 the full run starts only once the quick check finds nothing broken. expected_benefit.uncertainty: Loading every model once costs time (about 20 models at seconds to a minute each; Flash-Next's weights load about 30 s); a break that shows only deep in a long measurement still shows only there.

findings.title: Give the loop a finish line: no full scorecard run while known code fixes are open

sources.symbol: turn contract: a turn ends only when the plan is EMPTY
SelectValidation: every active cell 'run: re-acquired every cycle'
measurePhases: preflight, lanes, cells, publication; one broken cell marks the whole run broken
decline filing: one scorecard-regressed row per worsened cell

findings.evidence: The loop ends a turn only when the plan is empty. Each published scorecard files a row for every cell (about 110 cells, up to 7 measures each) worse than its earlier readings past its noise allowance, and a serving or memory row closes only on stored readings the next run refreshes, so each fix waits on a full run of about 9 hours (5h30m lanes, about 3h15m cells), and that run files rows again, some from machine state rather than code (Flash-Next's weight upload 28 s at 21:00 and 36 s at 21:40 on 2026-10-30, same code). A run passes only when every cell passes: 11 of the 12 runs since 2026-10-12 ended 'cells did not pass'. Since 2026-10-12: 917 commits, 12 runs, 8 scorecards; 25 plan items open, 10 filed by scorecards. An empty plan is unreachable by construction. Yet a row's check already reads the store's attempts, so a fix closes on its own model's measurement: the Qwen3.5-4B throughput row (8ce06a06d) and Flash-Next's first request (eacf5f6d3) closed that way on 2026-10-30 before any run.
findings.recommended_change: Owner 2026-10-31: do not run the whole scorecard until the code is fixed. (0) loop -improve refuses to start while the plan holds open code rows, unless code every model runs changed or the owner asks for a run; each fix closes by measuring only its own model; one full run confirms the finished list; pushes follow landings, not runs. (1) A finish line: a target list the owner approves (models, measures, levels); until set, today's open rows' targets plus 'hold within noise' for every other cell, and nothing added except a regression a change caused or an owner addition. (2) A landing measures the cells of the models it touches and stores them, and its row closes on them. (3) The scorecard is a report assembled from stored measurements, not a gate; see SQA-266. (4) A new row only where a change caused it: the cell's model files, code identity or recipe changed since its last reading; a worsening without such a change is no regression, since nothing changed that could break it: either nothing is broken, or the measure is broken (it reads differently on identical inputs) and the measure is fixed; it is never filed as a row against the model. (5) A broken cell marks only its own model broken, never the run.
findings.displaced_surface: The whole-plan-empty stop condition, the full run as the only closer of serving rows, and the push rule tied to measurement runs.
findings.impact: Without it the loop alternates fix, 9-hour run and newly filed rows indefinitely, and the owner sees days of testing with no end.

expected_benefit.outcome: Rows close in minutes on their own model's measurement; a full run happens once per finished list or when shared code changes; the loop reports done when the targets are met.
expected_benefit.uncertainty: Timing cells are noisy; a single-model closure must use the same three-attempt median the scorecard uses.

findings.likely_effort: Moderate: a launch refusal in loop -improve, a target list record, change-attribution in decline filing, and a broken cell marking only its own model.
findings.plan_coverage: No plan row covers the stop condition or run launching; lane-cost and stale-cells covered parts of the run's cost and truth.
